item.text: {"verdicts":[{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0009-R05-E006","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"Egypt reported that foreigners had the right to enter the labour market subject to legal restrictions. In 2020, 29,137 foreigners received first-time work permits, 33,242 work permits were renewed, and 18,332 foreigners were working in violation of the law; ministerial decrees enabled such workers to regularize their situation.","notes":["The excerpt does not state that all 18,332 people regularized their status; it identifies them as foreigners working in violation of the law and says ministerial decrees enabled regularization."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0009-R05-E007","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0009-R05-E008","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"Mental-health services had been integrated into 400 primary health-care units in areas with high concentrations of refugees; capacity-building was offered to medical staff, and health-care campaigns had expanded to include refugees and asylum-seekers, including hepatitis C, anti-polio, obesity, anaemia, and dwarfism initiatives.","notes":["The excerpt states 400 units, not 40.","The excerpt supports the listed initiatives and staff capacity-building but does not establish outcomes."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0009-R05-E009","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]}]}
